```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true"), collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

bayescompR runs models written in the BUGS language without JAGS, OpenBUGS,
WinBUGS, MultiBUGS or NIMBLE. The model is compiled and sampled in R. Code
written for R2jags, rjags, R2OpenBUGS or NIMBLE runs after replacing
`library(R2jags)` (or the others) with `library(bayescompR)`. The draws come
from the same posterior as the original programs give; the random numbers
differ.

```{r setup}
library(bayescompR)
```

## R2jags

```{r}
model <- function() {
  for (i in 1:N) {
    r[i] ~ dbin(p[i], n[i])
    logit(p[i]) <- alpha + beta * x[i]
  }
  alpha ~ dnorm(0, 1.0E-4)
  beta ~ dnorm(0, 1.0E-4)
}
data <- list(r = c(1, 4, 9, 13), n = c(20, 20, 20, 20), x = c(-1, 0, 1, 2), N = 4)
fit <- jags(data, NULL, c("alpha", "beta"), model, n.chains = 3, n.iter = 2000, jags.seed = 1)
fit
```

`fit$BUGSoutput` holds `sims.list`, `sims.array`, `sims.matrix`, `summary`,
`mean`, `sd`, `median`, `last.values`, `DIC` and `pD`, as in R2jags. DIC
uses R2jags's penalty: half the mean within-chain variance of the deviance.

## rjags

```{r}
m <- jags.model(textConnection("model {
  for (i in 1:N) { y[i] ~ dnorm(mu, tau) }
  mu ~ dnorm(0, 1.0E-4)
  tau ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
}"), data = list(y = c(1.2, 0.8, 1.9, 1.1, 1.4), N = 5), n.chains = 2, seed = 1)
update(m, 1000)
s <- coda.samples(m, c("mu", "tau"), n.iter = 2000)
summary(do.call(rbind, s))
```

`coda.samples()` returns an `mcmc.list`, so the functions of the coda
package work on it.

## R2OpenBUGS, WinBUGS and MultiBUGS

`bugs()` takes the arguments of `R2OpenBUGS::bugs()`. Model, data and initial
values can be files in OpenBUGS's formats, including rectangular data:

```{r}
dir <- tempfile(); dir.create(dir)
writeLines("model {
  for (i in 1:N) { y[i] ~ dpois(lambda[i])  log(lambda[i]) <- a + b * x[i] }
  a ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  b ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
}", file.path(dir, "model.txt"))
writeLines("list(N = 5)", file.path(dir, "data1.txt"))
writeLines("x[] y[]\n-2 1\n-1 2\n0 4\n1 6\n2 11\nEND", file.path(dir, "data2.txt"))
fit <- bugs(c("data1.txt", "data2.txt"), NULL, c("a", "b"), n.iter = 2000, model.file = "model.txt",
            n.chains = 2, working.directory = dir)
fit$summary
```

Initial values not given are drawn from the priors, as OpenBUGS's gen inits
does. DIC uses OpenBUGS's `pD`: the mean deviance minus the deviance at the
posterior means.

## NIMBLE

```{r}
code <- nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:N) y[i] ~ dnorm(mu, sd = sigma)
  mu ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
  sigma ~ dunif(0, 10)
})
out <- nimbleMCMC(code, constants = list(N = 5), data = list(y = c(1.1, 0.4, 1.8, 0.9, 1.3)),
                  niter = 3000, nburnin = 1000, nchains = 2, setSeed = 1, summary = TRUE)
out$summary$all.chains
```

`nimbleModel()`, `configureMCMC()`, `buildMCMC()`, `compileNimble()` and
`runMCMC()` work too. `compileNimble()` returns its argument: nothing is
compiled to C++.

## Samplers

Each unobserved node is updated in turn, given the others:

* conjugate updates for gamma (precisions, rates), beta, Dirichlet and
  Wishart nodes, and for normal nodes whose children are linear in them
  (regression coefficients and random effects), drawn as one block;
* metropolized Gibbs for discrete nodes with a small support: the
  conditional probabilities are enumerated and a value other than the
  current one is proposed, which moves more often than plain Gibbs;
* elliptical slice sampling for multivariate normal nodes that are not
  partly observed, moving the whole vector at once;
* slice sampling for the other nodes, with widths adapted during the
  burn-in to four times the mean jump; and
* special updates for latent multinomial counts.

Nodes that do not depend on each other are updated together, which keeps
large hierarchical models fast in R.

## What is supported

The language of JAGS 5 and OpenBUGS 3.2: stochastic and logical nodes, link
functions on the left side, `for` loops, truncation with `T()`, censoring
with `C()` and `I()`, `cut()`, data transformations (a `data` block, or
logical nodes of data only), missing values, and all distributions and
functions of the two manuals that do not need a program of their own.
NIMBLE's dialect adds named parameters (`dnorm(mu, sd = s)`) and its
alternative parameterizations.

Not supported:

* user-defined `nimbleFunction`s and custom samplers;
* ordering constraints and cyclic models (`dsum`-type stochastic sums), as in
  the Inhalers, Jama, StVeit and Ice examples of OpenBUGS;
* graph functionals such as `cumulative()` and `D()` (ordinary
  differential equations);
* Wishart nodes that are not conjugate;
* stochastic nodes inside `data` blocks; and
* `pD = TRUE` in `jags()` (the DIC of `dic.samples()`).

## Validation

`validation/bugs/validate-examples.R` in the source repository runs 45 of
the OpenBUGS Examples (volumes 1 to 3) and compares the posterior means of
271 nodes with the estimates OpenBUGS 3.2.3 reports for them. A mean passes
when it is within 4 combined Monte Carlo standard errors of OpenBUGS's
estimate or within a tenth of its posterior standard deviation. All 45
models pass. Fire, Stagnantc and t-df have no reported estimates, and Ice,
Inhalers, Jama, StVeit and Sixcomp use features listed above as not
supported.
